answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that flows like a river: every agent must lock a small, slashable bond before it can trade, and each completed job earns a signed receipt, a quill mark on its public record, that only accrues with time and real work. A sybil attacker must fund a fresh bond per identity, and juniper-slow growth means new identities cannot instantly buy trust; faking a hundred agents costs a hundred bonds and yields no history, so the attack costs more than it can extract.
